title: Merge conflicts
summary: Read conflict markers, decide what the code should really be, and finish or abort a merge.

steps.title: What a conflict looks like
body: When both sides change the same lines differently, Git stops the merge and writes **both** versions into the file:
```text
public decimal Shipping(decimal total)
return total > 50 ? 0 : 4.99m;
return total >= 40 ? 0 : 3.99m;
>>>>>>> feature
- Between `<<<<<<< HEAD` and `=======`: **ours**, the branch you are on.
- Between `=======` and `>>>>>>> feature`: **theirs**, the branch you are merging in.
`git status` lists the file under *Unmerged paths* (`UU` in `git status -s`). The merge is paused until you resolve every file.

steps.prompt: In the conflict above, you were on `main` and ran `git merge feature`. Which line came from `main`?
options: Neither: Git invented a combined version
steps.explain: The top half is always HEAD, the branch you are on. (During a **rebase** it is reversed in feel: HEAD is the branch being built, the upstream, and *theirs* is your commit being replayed.)

steps.title: Resolving
body: Resolving means editing the file into what the code **should** be, which may be ours, theirs, or something new:
```text
public decimal Shipping(decimal total)
return total >= 50 ? 0 : 3.99m;   // product decided: threshold 50, new price
Then:
```text
git add Shipping.cs          # marks this file resolved
git status                   # any files still unmerged?
git commit                   # finishes the merge (message is pre-filled)
Changed your mind? `git merge --abort` puts everything back as it was before the merge.
> **Tip:** Set `git config --global merge.conflictStyle zdiff3`. Conflicts then also show the **base** version between `|||||||` and `=======`, so you can see what each side actually changed.

steps.prompt: Arrange the steps to resolve a merge conflict in `Cart.cs` and finish the merge.
lines: Edit Cart.cs: keep the right code, delete the <<<<<<< ======= >>>>>>> lines
steps.explain: Merge, see what conflicted, resolve, **build and test** (a conflict-free merge can still be broken, and a resolved one even more so), mark resolved, then commit.

steps.prompt: You resolved only `Cart.cs` and ran `git add Cart.cs`. `Order.cs` still contains conflict markers. What does `git status -s` print? (Name order.)
code: git merge feature        # conflicts in Cart.cs and Order.cs
steps.explain: `git add` marks Cart.cs resolved (its merged content is staged). `UU` means *unmerged, both modified*: Order.cs still needs work before you can commit.

steps.prompt: A conflict-free merge compiled, but the tests now fail. How can that be?
options: One branch renamed a method and the other added a new call to the old name, in different lines; textually no conflict, semantically broken
Git merges are never wrong if there is no conflict
Tests do not run after a merge
steps.explain: Git merges **text**, not meaning. That is why you build and test after every merge, and why CI runs on the merge result, not just the branch.

steps.prompt: Match the marker or command to its meaning.
pairs: start of the version on your current branch
end of the incoming branch's version
give up and restore the pre-merge state

steps.prompt: Complete the commands: during a conflict, take *our* version of `package.lock` wholesale, then mark it resolved.
steps.explain: `git checkout --ours <file>` / `--theirs <file>` take one side for a whole file. Handy for generated files, which you then regenerate.

steps.title: Three-way merge of lines
prompt: Write a line-level three-way merge. The three versions have the **same number of lines** (only edits, no insertions), so line `i` of each corresponds.
`Merge3(baseLines, ours, theirs)` returns the merged lines. For each `i`:
- ours == base: only theirs changed, take theirs;
- theirs == base: only ours changed, take ours;
- otherwise emit a conflict block of five lines:
starter: static List<string> Merge3(string[] baseLines, string[] ours, string[] theirs)
solution: static List<string> Merge3(string[] baseLines, string[] ours, string[] theirs)
string b = baseLines[i], o = ours[i], t = theirs[i];
hints: Check `o == t` first: it covers "nobody changed it" and "both made the same change".
Then `o == b` means take `t`, and `t == b` means take `o`.
Anything left is a conflict: add the five lines.
template: Dojo.Eq("one side each, no conflict", new List<string> { "a = 2", "b = 5", "c = 1" }, Merge3(b, new[] { "a = 1", "b = 5", "c = 1" }, new[] { "a = 2", "b = 1", "c = 1" }));
Dojo.Eq("same change on both sides", new List<string> { "a = 9", "b = 1", "c = 1" }, Merge3(b, new[] { "a = 9", "b = 1", "c = 1" }, new[] { "a = 9", "b = 1", "c = 1" }));
Dojo.Eq("conflict block", new List<string> { "a = 1", "<<<<<<< ours", "b = 2", "=======", "b = 3", ">>>>>>> theirs", "c = 1" },
Dojo.Eq("empty files", new List<string>(), Merge3(new string[0], new string[0], new string[0]));
